questions.stem: What extra feature does a reaction profile show that a simple energy level diagram does not?

options.text: How the energy changes during the course of the reaction
options.explanation: The curve between the levels is the added information a profile carries.

options.text: The temperature of the reaction mixture
options.explanation: Temperature never appears on energy diagrams.

options.text: The concentration of the reactants
options.explanation: Concentration belongs to rate experiments, not profiles.

options.text: The time taken for the reaction
options.explanation: Profiles show energy against progress, not time.

questions.stem: What does the rise from reactants to the peak of the curve represent?

options.text: The activation energy required to start the reaction
options.explanation: That initial climb is the minimum energy particles need to react.

options.text: The overall enthalpy change
options.explanation: The enthalpy change is reactants to products, not to the peak.

options.text: The energy released by the products
options.explanation: Release happens on the way down, not on the initial climb.

options.text: The activation energy of the reverse reaction only
options.explanation: The forward barrier is the one drawn from the reactant level.

questions.stem: On an exothermic profile, which way does the enthalpy arrow point and what sign carries?

options.text: Downwards with a negative value
options.explanation: Products sit lower, so the overall arrow descends and ΔH is negative.

options.text: Upwards with a positive value
options.explanation: That is the endothermic profile.

options.text: Downwards with a positive value
options.explanation: A downward arrow with a positive sign contradicts itself.

options.text: Upwards with a negative value
options.explanation: Neither half matches exothermic behaviour.

questions.stem: Two reactions share the same enthalpy change but reaction X has a higher peak. What follows?

options.text: X needs more energy to get going, so more heat is needed to start it
options.explanation: A taller barrier means a harder start even when the overall change matches.

options.text: X releases more energy overall
options.explanation: The overall change is stated to be the same.

options.text: X must be endothermic and the other exothermic
options.explanation: Equal enthalpy changes mean both point the same way.

options.text: X has no activation energy
options.explanation: Every reaction has some barrier; X's is simply taller.

questions.stem: What is the definition of activation energy?

options.text: The minimum energy that reacting particles must have for a reaction to occur
options.explanation: That threshold is exactly what the profile peak measures.

options.text: The total energy stored in all the bonds of the reactants
options.explanation: Stored energy is not the threshold concept.

options.text: The energy released when products form
options.explanation: Release belongs to the product side of the profile.

options.text: The energy needed to raise the temperature by one degree
options.explanation: That is specific heat capacity.

questions.stem: How does a catalyst appear on a reaction profile?

options.text: As a second curve with a lower peak between the same reactant and product levels
options.explanation: The alternative pathway is drawn lower while the endpoints stay fixed.

options.text: As a deeper valley below the reactant level
options.explanation: The route still climbs to a peak; it is just a smaller one.

options.text: As a new product level lower than before
options.explanation: Product levels are unchanged by catalysis.

options.text: As a vertical line at the start
options.explanation: Catalysts change the pathway shape, not the axes.

questions.stem: Why does lowering the peak increase the rate?

options.text: A greater proportion of molecules now have sufficient energy for an effective collision
options.explanation: The smaller hurdle converts average collisions into successful ones.

options.text: Because the molecules themselves become more energetic
options.explanation: Molecule energies are unchanged; the requirement drops.

options.text: Because the products are more stable
options.explanation: Product stability is identical with or without the catalyst.

options.text: Because the reactant level falls
options.explanation: The reactant level never moves.

questions.stem: What happens to the overall enthalpy change when a catalyst is added?

options.text: It is unchanged, because the start and finish levels are the same
options.explanation: Catalysts alter the route, never the endpoints.

options.text: It becomes more negative
options.explanation: The drop between levels is fixed.

options.text: It becomes positive
options.explanation: The direction of the overall change is untouched.

options.text: It halves, because the barrier fell
options.explanation: Barrier and overall change are different quantities.

questions.stem: A reaction occurs readily at room temperature. What does its profile look like?

options.text: It has a low activation peak, so little energy is needed to begin
options.explanation: Ready reactions correspond to small barriers.

options.text: It has no peak at all
options.explanation: Every reaction has some barrier to clear.

options.text: It has a very high peak
options.explanation: A high peak would make the reaction reluctant, not ready.

options.text: Its product level sits above its reactant level
options.explanation: Readiness says nothing about the sign of the change.

questions.stem: The activation energy for a particular reaction is described as what kind of quantity?

options.text: A fixed value for that reaction, unchanged by how fast the reaction is run
options.explanation: The barrier is a property of the reaction and its pathway.

options.text: A value that grows as the reaction proceeds
options.explanation: The barrier is set by the pathway, not by progress.

options.text: A value that depends on the amount of product formed
options.explanation: Yield does not set the barrier.

options.text: A value that changes with the colour of the mixture
options.explanation: Colour has no bearing on the barrier.
